paragraphs: 3D-LLM extends language models with information about three-dimensional scenes. The motivation is that reasoning about text or images alone does not ground a model in spatial relationships, physical layouts, or possible interactions with objects. The proposed models accept point clouds and associated features, supporting tasks such as scene descriptions, questions about scenes, navigation, and dialogue.

The training pipeline connects existing visual-language capabilities to 3D inputs. A feature extractor obtains 3D features from rendered views, and existing two-dimensional vision-language models provide the backbone. A localization mechanism helps represent spatial information. The authors also design three prompting mechanisms to collect more than 300,000 examples connecting 3D scenes with language tasks.

On ScanQA, the model exceeds the reported leading baselines, including a reported 9% improvement in BLEU-1. Tests on held-in datasets also favor it over 2D vision-language models for captioning, task composition, and dialogue. These results support the usefulness of explicit 3D information for the evaluated tasks; qualitative examples suggest additional capabilities beyond those comparisons.
neurips-2023-3d-llm-injecting-the-3d-wor.tldr: 3D-LLM adds point-cloud features and spatial localization to vision-language backbones to improve language tasks grounded in 3D scenes.

paragraphs: Marginals summarize a dataset over selected attributes, and releasing noisy versions can protect confidentiality while supporting later analysis. Matrix mechanisms provide unbiased noisy answers to these kinds of linear queries. The paper introduces ResidualPlanner, a mechanism designed to choose how accurately different marginals are released when the added noise is Gaussian.

Its central contribution combines optimality with flexibility in the objective being optimized. ResidualPlanner supports many losses expressible as convex functions of marginal variances, whereas the cited earlier approach supported one predefined objective. This makes the accuracy allocation responsive to different loss functions within that mathematical class, rather than requiring every release to use the same criterion.

The abstract reports optimization in seconds on large settings where HDMM runs out of memory, and completion in a couple of minutes for datasets with 100 attributes. ResidualPlanner also efficiently calculates variances and covariances for individual marginals. Those quantities describe uncertainty and relationships between errors, making the mechanism useful both for planning a release and understanding its resulting noise.
neurips-2023-an-optimal-and-scalable-mat.tldr: ResidualPlanner optimally allocates Gaussian noise for marginals under a broad class of convex variance-based losses while scaling to large datasets.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a bone’s three-dimensional shape from two perpendicular X-rays has attracted many deep learning approaches. Comparing them is difficult when studies use different anatomies, patient groups, and private datasets. This paper establishes a shared benchmark so that reconstruction models can be evaluated on comparable data and on outcomes relevant to clinical use.

The platform supplies reference implementations of eight models, tools to collect and preprocess six public datasets, and automatic extraction of clinical parameters and landmarks. Its evaluations cover four anatomies and include fractured bones, implants, changes in the population being evaluated, and errors in clinical measurements. This broadens comparison beyond a single image segmentation score.

Attention-based models that capture global spatial relationships tend to perform better across the evaluated datasets and anatomies. Ribs prove substantially harder than femur, hip, and spine. The authors also find that aggregate results can overestimate performance for clinically relevant subgroups, and better Dice scores do not always yield better clinical measurements. The findings make the choice of evaluation target consequential.
neurips-2023-benchmarking-encoder-decode.tldr: A shared benchmark compares eight X-ray-to-3D reconstruction models and shows why clinical measurements and subgroup results matter alongside segmentation scores.

paragraphs: BioMassters addresses the problem of estimating above-ground forest biomass over large areas. Biomass matters for understanding forests as carbon sinks. Field surveys and airborne LiDAR can provide reliable estimates, but applying those methods at large scale can be expensive and difficult. Satellite observations offer a way to investigate more extensive mapping.

The paper contributes a public benchmark dataset and data challenge built around satellite observations collected over time. It combines Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 MSI data, using airborne LiDAR information from the Finnish Forest Centre as the reference. The research question is how effectively deep learning can use these multiple observation types and their time series to estimate biomass.

The performance of the three leading models indicates potential for accurate, higher-resolution biomass maps. The contribution therefore includes both a common evaluation resource and initial evidence that the available satellite information can support useful predictions. Public access to the dataset and winning implementations makes those approaches available for further investigation within the benchmark.
neurips-2023-biomassters-a-benchmark-dat.tldr: BioMassters provides satellite time series and LiDAR references for benchmarking deep learning approaches to large-scale forest biomass estimation.

paragraphs: Averaging peer-review scores can reduce random noise, but it can still produce unfair rankings when reviewers have different noise levels or share systematic biases. Signals such as author identity or proof length can influence ratings without reliably reflecting paper quality. Because these judgments are subjective and unverifiable, correcting them is especially challenging.

The proposed procedure asks reviewers to predict the scores that other reviewers will give. It then uses those predictions to calibrate the ratings in a single round, without historical data or prior information. The key assumption is that reviewers adjust their predictions according to the noise. The theoretical results depend on this relationship between predictions and noisy judgments.

Under that assumption, the calibrated scores yield more robust rankings than simple averages despite varying noise and biases. The authors show that ranking error probability tends to zero as reviewer numbers grow and is substantially lower than averaging when reviewer numbers are small. The contribution is a conditional way to extract useful calibration information from reviewers’ expectations.
neurips-2023-calibrating-cheap-signals-i.tldr: Reviewer predictions of others’ scores enable prior-free calibration with stronger ranking guarantees when those predictions adjust appropriately to noise.

paragraphs: Self-supervised learning can struggle when a dataset contains many examples of a few categories and few examples of many others. The paper attributes part of this problem to objectives that spread individual samples uniformly through the representation space. With uneven category frequencies, common categories can dominate that space while rare categories become poorly distinguished.

Geometric Harmonization changes the emphasis toward uniformity at the category level. It measures population statistics in the learned embedding space and derives adjustments for individual examples. These adjustments constrain the expansion of common categories and aim to prevent rare categories from collapsing. The approach retains the self-supervised setting and is designed to integrate into existing methods at low cost.

The intended benefit is better treatment of minority categories with almost no harm to majority categories. Results across benchmark datasets support the method’s effectiveness and tolerance of strongly skewed distributions. The broader implication is that how representation space is distributed matters: spreading samples evenly can still leave categories unevenly represented when their sample counts differ.
neurips-2023-combating-representation-le.tldr: Geometric Harmonization adjusts self-supervised representations to reduce domination by frequent categories and collapse among rare ones.

paragraphs: This paper studies the shape of policy optimization objectives in reinforcement learning. A superlevel set contains all policy parameters whose objective value reaches a chosen threshold. The authors prove that these sets are connected in the tabular setting and for policies represented by a particular class of neural networks. Thus, qualifying parameters do not split into disconnected regions.

They also establish a stronger property called equiconnectedness for the objective viewed jointly through policy parameters and rewards. This structure becomes useful in minimax problems, where one side chooses a policy while the other can act adversarially. The authors prove minimax equality for programs that are convex on one side and equiconnected on the other.

An identified class of robust reinforcement learning problems with adversarial reward attacks has exactly this structure. The general theorem therefore establishes minimax equality, and the associated equilibrium result, for that class. The contribution connects the geometry of policy optimization to guarantees about adversarial decision-making, with the neural-network and robust-learning results applying to the classes studied.
neurips-2023-connected-superlevel-set-in.tldr: Connected policy-objective superlevel sets and a stronger equiconnectedness property yield minimax guarantees for a class of robust reinforcement learning problems.

paragraphs: The paper builds generative neural fields from combinations of smaller implicit neural networks. These basis networks provide reusable components, while latent coefficients determine how they are combined for a particular instance. The method learns both the basis networks and the coefficients, using either meta-learning or an auto-decoding approach.

A central design goal is to increase the capacity of the generative model without enlarging the network needed at inference. Adding basis networks expands the available components, while weighted model averaging keeps the inference network small. This separation makes sampling efficient in latency and memory footprint, according to the abstract, while allowing the learned collection of basis networks to grow.

To generate new instances, the authors adapt a denoising diffusion probabilistic model to sample the latent mixture coefficients. Those sampled coefficients then specify a new neural field. Experiments report competitive generation across images, voxel data, and NeRF scenes without elaborate designs for each modality. The results support the combination framework as a shared approach across several kinds of visual data.
neurips-2023-generative-neural-fields-by.tldr: Mixtures of implicit basis networks enable generative neural fields with expandable capacity and compact inference, using diffusion to sample mixture coefficients.

paragraphs: Virtual try-on must change a person’s clothing while handling flexible garment shapes and the close interaction between clothing and body appearance. The paper identifies two obstacles: auxiliary training tasks can introduce unsuitable prior knowledge, and deformation methods can fail to capture garment-body relationships. Both can interfere with realistic clothing alignment.

USC-PFN uses a single generator within a circular self-cycle consistency architecture. Training takes real, unpaired garment-person images as inputs, avoiding the problematic prior knowledge introduced at the input by auxiliary tasks. The framework supports self-supervised cycle training with a general generator, simplifying the arrangement compared with approaches that depend on teacher knowledge or two generators.

The method also uses a Markov Random Field to model garment deformation more naturally. This addresses geometry alongside the changes to the training structure, rather than relying on appearance translation alone. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance on a popular virtual try-on benchmark. Together, the results support a simpler training design combined with explicit attention to realistic non-rigid deformation.
neurips-2023-greatness-in-simplicity-uni.tldr: USC-PFN combines single-generator self-cycle training with Markov Random Field deformation modeling for parser-free virtual try-on.

paragraphs: Self-play generates training experience by having a learner interact with copies of itself. The resulting strategy may encounter very different opponents after training. Two-player constant-sum games offer equilibrium-based protection against this mismatch, but multiplayer games do not generally inherit that guarantee. This paper identifies structural conditions under which a broader guarantee becomes possible.

The first condition is that the multiplayer game approximately decomposes into pairwise constant-sum games. The second, called subgame stability, requires approximate equilibria of the overall game to remain boundedly close to equilibria in the pairwise subgames. Together, these conditions connect whole-game behavior to the more controlled structure of two-player interactions.

For games satisfying those conditions, self-play with any no-external-regret algorithm produces strategies with bounded vulnerability. This bounds exposure to different opponents after training rather than asserting universal protection for multiplayer self-play. Experiments on Leduc poker demonstrate the findings. The contribution is a sufficient structural basis for guarantees that applies to a broad algorithm class when the game has the required properties.
neurips-2023-guarantees-for-self-play-in.tldr: Approximate constant-sum pairwise structure and subgame stability give no-external-regret self-play bounded vulnerability in certain multiplayer games.

paragraphs: When a reward arrives long after an action, a reinforcement learning agent must determine which earlier decisions deserve credit. Reward redistribution assigns observed returns back to individual time steps. This paper makes that reassignment interpretable by explicitly modeling the causal contributions of states and actions, while preserving policy invariance.

The proposed Generative Return Decomposition framework begins with a causal account of how immediate Markovian rewards and whole-trajectory returns arise. It identifies the unobserved rewards and causal relationships in that process. It then uses the identified model to construct a compact representation for policy training, concentrating learning on a favorable subspace of the agent’s state space.

The theoretical contribution establishes identifiability of the hidden Markovian reward function, causal structure, and causal models in the studied formulation. Experiments report better performance than state-of-the-art methods, and visualizations illustrate interpretability. The framework therefore links two goals: giving delayed feedback a more explicit causal explanation and using that explanation to guide policy optimization through a focused representation.
neurips-2023-interpretable-reward-redist.tldr: Generative Return Decomposition uses causal models to explain delayed rewards and construct compact representations for policy learning while preserving policy invariance.

paragraphs: Homomorphic encryption allows graph convolutional networks to process encrypted client data, but the computation can be expensive. LinGCN targets multiplication depth, a central source of overhead in this setting. It coordinates changes to the network and the encrypted execution procedure so that privacy-preserving inference requires fewer multiplication levels.

The framework learns where nonlinear operations should remain at individual nodes, jointly training those structural choices with model weights. It replaces selected activations with trainable second-order polynomials and uses two-level distillation from an all-ReLU teacher to improve convergence. An enhanced encryption implementation then fuses operators more finely around the node-specific activations, further reducing multiplication-level consumption.

On the NTU-XVIEW skeleton joint dataset, LinGCN achieves a reported 14.2-fold latency improvement over CryptoGCN while retaining approximately 75% accuracy. A larger configuration reaches 85.78% accuracy with 6,371-second latency, reported as a 10.47% accuracy improvement over CryptoGCN. These results demonstrate different accuracy-latency configurations and support the value of designing the network structure together with its encrypted execution.
neurips-2023-lingcn-structural-linearize.tldr: LinGCN jointly redesigns graph-network nonlinearities and encrypted execution to reduce multiplication depth and improve homomorphic inference performance.

paragraphs: MAViL learns representations from paired audio and video through three complementary self-supervised tasks. The first reconstructs hidden portions of the raw sound and visual inputs. The second uses contrastive learning, with masking, both within each modality and between them. Together, these tasks train the model to recover information and connect related audio-visual representations.

The third task is self-training: the model predicts aligned, contextualized representations learned through the first two objectives. This adds a target built from learned audio-video structure alongside reconstruction of raw inputs. The approach therefore combines learning from missing content, relationships within and across modalities, and representations produced by the training process itself.

The authors report state-of-the-art classification results of 53.3 mAP on AudioSet and 67.1% accuracy on VGGSound, surpassing the compared self-supervised and externally supervised models. Pre-training also improves multimodal retrieval and the representations of audio and video individually. Those individual gains remain when fine-tuning and inference use only one modality, showing that joint training can benefit later single-modality tasks.
neurips-2023-mavil-masked-audio-video-le.tldr: MAViL combines masked reconstruction, contrastive learning, and self-training to improve joint audio-video representations and each modality used alone.

paragraphs: This paper adapts the nearest-neighbour rule to contextual bandits, where decisions depend on context and feedback is limited to the chosen action. The algorithm handles a fully adversarial setting without assumptions about how the data are generated. Its aim is to combine that broad setting with computational efficiency as the sequence of decisions grows.

The efficiency guarantee depends on access to a sufficiently fast data structure for adaptive nearest-neighbour search, potentially approximate, such as a navigating net. With that support, each trial takes time polylogarithmic in both the number of trials and the number of actions, while storage is quasi-linear. The search machinery is therefore an explicit condition behind the computational claim.

The authors establish generic regret bounds and examine their implications for stochastic bandits in Euclidean space. A further result concerns online classification with stochastic labels: under certain conditions, the algorithm achieves sublinear regret while retrieving only one neighbour per trial. This gives a conditional alternative to retrieving multiple neighbours, alongside the main adversarial bandit contribution.
neurips-2023-nearest-neighbour-with-band.tldr: A nearest-neighbour contextual bandit algorithm handles adversarial data and achieves efficient operation when paired with a sufficiently fast adaptive search structure.

paragraphs: The paper asks what happens to kernel-based learning when the number of input variables grows without bound. Its motivation comes from interacting particle systems, where descriptions may involve very many variables. This is a mean-field limit of the learning problem, distinct from simply collecting more training examples for a fixed input description.

The authors extend the theory of limiting kernels and their associated reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. They then establish approximation results, including a representer theorem. These steps provide mathematical foundations for describing which functions can be represented and how kernel-based solutions behave as the input system grows.

The analysis proceeds to statistical learning, focusing on support vector machines. It establishes mean-field convergence for both empirical solutions based on data and infinite-sample solutions, together with convergence of their risks. The significance is a rigorous connection between finite-variable kernel learning and its limiting formulation. The contribution supplies theoretical tools for large-scale problems and develops a form of learning-problem limit that the authors identify as previously unexplored.
neurips-2023-on-kernel-based-statistical.tldr: The paper establishes mean-field limits for kernels, support vector machine solutions, and their risks as the number of input variables grows.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to replenish multiple products over time when a manager has only partial historical information. The objective is to minimize cumulative losses across the sequence of decisions. Its motivation is to move beyond inventory models built around a standard loss form, fixed dynamics, and independent demands drawn from an unchanged distribution.

The authors propose MaxCOSD, an online algorithm with provable guarantees for more general inventory problems. The covered settings include non-independent or changing demand and stateful dynamics, where the inventory situation carries consequences forward. Perishability is one stated example. Through online convex optimization, the work brings these sequential features into the learning problem.

The guarantees are accompanied by what the authors call non-degeneracy assumptions on the demand process. They argue that such assumptions are necessary to make learning possible. The contribution therefore broadens the demand and inventory behavior that can be handled while retaining explicit conditions on the environment. Its central finding is that useful guarantees can extend beyond the usual independent-demand formulation.
neurips-2023-online-inventory-problems-b.tldr: MaxCOSD provides online inventory-control guarantees beyond independent-demand models, including stateful dynamics, under demand non-degeneracy assumptions.

paragraphs: Simulation-based inference estimates model parameters when the likelihood cannot be evaluated tractably. Approximate Bayesian Computation approaches this through likelihood approximation, while Sequential Neural Posterior Estimation directly learns a posterior. This paper introduces Pseudo-Likelihood Inference to bring neural approximation into the former approach and improve its competitiveness on demanding system-identification problems.

PLI uses integral probability metrics to construct a smooth likelihood kernel. Its bandwidth adapts through information-theoretic trust regions, providing a controlled way to update that kernel during inference. The resulting formulation permits gradient-based optimization of neural posteriors, accepts multiple observations, and does not depend on summary statistics. These properties connect the likelihood-approximation approach with flexible neural optimization.

The method is evaluated on four established simulation-based inference benchmarks and a highly dynamic physical system. The authors report improved performance relative to SNPE when more data are available, with particular advantages for stochastic simulations and posterior distributions containing multiple modes. The findings support PLI as a useful alternative in those tested settings, especially when inference must use several observations.
neurips-2023-pseudo-likelihood-inference.tldr: Pseudo-Likelihood Inference brings neural optimization into approximate Bayesian computation through an adaptive smooth likelihood kernel that supports multiple observations.

paragraphs: Bayesian optimization searches for good decisions when rewards come from a complicated black-box function. Its cumulative regret measures the reward lost over repeated choices. Classical algorithms face a stated lower bound growing with the square root of the number of iterations. Earlier quantum improvements addressed multi-armed or linear bandits, leaving more general nonlinear functions outside their scope.

The paper introduces Q-GP-UCB, a quantum Gaussian-process upper-confidence-bound algorithm. The authors establish a regret upper bound that grows only polylogarithmically with the iteration count, improving on the stated classical lower bound in the quantum setting. A new confidence-ellipsoid analysis also gives its linear-kernel version a smaller regret bound than the previous quantum linear UCB algorithm.

Simulations and an experiment on a real quantum computer examine whether the theoretical advantage could matter in practice. The abstract describes the evidence as showing potential practical relevance. The main contribution is therefore a stronger theoretical regret guarantee for quantum Bayesian optimization, accompanied by empirical exploration of that advantage rather than a universal practical speedup claim.
neurips-2023-quantum-bayesian-optimizati.tldr: Q-GP-UCB achieves a polylogarithmic quantum Bayesian optimization regret bound, with experiments suggesting potential practical relevance.

paragraphs: Community detection is harder to characterize when a graph contains groups of very different sizes. This paper studies that situation in the stochastic block model and introduces a simple algorithm based on singular value decomposition. Its goal is to recover communities without relying on restrictions that made earlier guarantees less suitable for highly uneven group sizes.

The analysis removes a previous requirement for a large gap in the possible community sizes. It also removes dependence of the recoverable community-size threshold on the total number of communities. Experimental comparisons complement these improvements. When probability parameters are constant, the authors show near-optimal recoverable sizes up to polylogarithmic factors, conditional on the planted clique conjecture.

The method also yields a clustering algorithm for a faulty-oracle setting that uses a sublinear number of queries. It can detect all sufficiently large clusters at roughly the square-root-of-n scale, with logarithmic factors suppressed, even alongside a linear number of small clusters. This extends recovery guarantees to settings where numerous small groups obstructed earlier efficient methods.
neurips-2023-recovering-unbalanced-commu.tldr: An SVD-based algorithm strengthens recovery guarantees for uneven graph communities and enables efficient faulty-oracle clustering despite many small groups.

paragraphs: SnapFusion targets the cost of running text-to-image diffusion models on mobile devices. Large networks and repeated denoising steps make conventional models computationally demanding, encouraging cloud execution. The paper presents an approach that reports generation in less than two seconds on mobile devices by reducing both network computation and the number of denoising iterations.

The architecture work identifies redundancy in the original model to produce a more efficient UNet. It also reduces image-decoder computation through data distillation. Alongside those changes, the authors improve step distillation through training strategies and regularization derived from classifier-free guidance. These components address the cost of each step and the number of steps needed.

On MS-COCO, the resulting model uses eight denoising steps and achieves better FID and CLIP scores than Stable Diffusion v1.5 using fifty steps. This provides evidence that the reported efficiency gains can coexist with strong measured output quality. The practical contribution is a route to fast generation on mobile devices, reducing the need for remote computation in that setting.
neurips-2023-snapfusion-text-to-image-di.tldr: SnapFusion combines efficient architecture and improved step distillation to report mobile text-to-image generation in under two seconds.

paragraphs: Winograd convolution speeds up convolution by performing calculations in a transformed domain. Quantization could reduce its cost further, but applying post-training quantization can severely reduce accuracy. Existing approaches also commonly quantize only element-wise multiplication, leaving substantial computation in the algorithm’s other stages at full precision.

The authors identify inconsistencies between transformation procedures and introduce PTQ-Aware Winograd to optimize those procedures together under one objective. They also investigate full quantization for faster Winograd variants with tile sizes of at least four. Factorized Scale Quantization addresses the large differences in numerical ranges within the transformed domain through a hardware-friendly scaling method.

The reported experiments show improved accuracy over an earlier Winograd post-training quantization method. With eight-bit quantization and tile size six, the abstract reports top-1 accuracy improvements of 8.27% for ResNet-18 and 5.38% for ResNet-34. The contribution combines broader coverage of quantized computation with joint treatment of the transformations and their numerical ranges, addressing both the efficiency opportunity and the observed accuracy problem.
neurips-2023-towards-efficient-and-accur.tldr: Joint transformation optimization and factorized scaling improve fully quantized Winograd convolution, with reported accuracy gains over earlier post-training quantization.

paragraphs: Normalization uses statistical descriptions of features and has become common in networks that manipulate image style. This paper explores its role in image enhancement, treating enhancement as a related transformation problem. It introduces Transition-Constant Normalization, a component intended to improve enhancement networks without adding learned parameters or computational cost.

TCN combines two normalization streams under an invertibility constraint with feature subsampling that respects the normalization constraint. The authors provide several ways to use the component: inserting it into enhancement networks, incorporating it into encoder-decoder downsampling, and building efficient architectures around it. This makes the proposed operation applicable at different points in a network’s design.

Experiments report consistent improvements across low-light enhancement, exposure correction, SDR-to-HDR translation, and dehazing. The abstract also reports applicability to pan-sharpening and medical segmentation. The findings support normalization as a useful design choice across the evaluated tasks, with the parameter-free, plug-and-play construction making the improvement accessible without a separate set of trainable normalization parameters.
neurips-2023-transition-constant-normali.tldr: Transition-Constant Normalization is a parameter-free component that reports consistent improvements across several image enhancement tasks without additional computational cost.

paragraphs: Expected Improvement helps Bayesian optimization choose where to evaluate an unknown objective next. Although widely used, its numerical values can vanish across large parts of the search space, making the acquisition function difficult to optimize. The paper argues that this problem contributes to inconsistent and often weaker-than-necessary performance.

The authors introduce LogEI, a family of reformulations whose optima are either identical or approximately equal to those of their original acquisition functions. The reformulations are substantially easier to optimize numerically. They address ordinary Expected Improvement and Expected Hypervolume Improvement, together with constrained, noisy, and parallel variants. The numerical difficulties generally worsen as observations, dimensions, or constraints increase.

Experiments show substantial gains over the corresponding original acquisition functions, with LogEI variants matching or exceeding recent state-of-the-art alternatives in the reported evaluations. This gives a different interpretation of some acquisition-function comparisons: performance depends on how successfully the selected criterion can actually be optimized. Improving numerical behavior can therefore improve the decisions made by an otherwise closely related optimization rule.
neurips-2023-unexpected-improvements-to-.tldr: LogEI reformulates Expected Improvement variants to avoid numerical failures while preserving identical or approximately equivalent optima.

paragraphs: Very long inputs remain expensive for Transformers, making tasks such as answering questions about books difficult to run efficiently. VCC addresses this by compressing the sequence into a much smaller representation at every layer. Its guiding observation is that, in many tasks, a small subset of tokens is especially relevant to the final prediction.

The authors call these important positions VIP-tokens. Compression is selected according to its effect on approximating their representations. This ties the treatment of the surrounding sequence to the information needed at the prediction-relevant tokens. The approach therefore directs computation according to the task’s important representations instead of preserving equal detail throughout a long input.

The reported comparisons show more than threefold compute-efficiency gains over competitive baselines at sequence lengths of 4,000 and 16,000 tokens, with competitive or better performance across many tasks. The authors also demonstrate scaling to 128,000 tokens or more with consistent accuracy improvements. These findings support selective compression when a relatively small set of tokens carries particular importance for the output.
neurips-2023-vcc-scaling-transformers-to.tldr: VCC compresses Transformer sequences around prediction-relevant tokens, improving efficiency and demonstrating scaling to 128,000 tokens or more.

paragraphs: A visual prompt generator connects image information to a language model, offering a relatively lightweight route to a multimodal system. Even so, training that connector can require substantial computation and data. This paper investigates whether an existing visual prompt generator can be transferred to another language model instead of being trained afresh.

The authors study transfers across language-model sizes and types, identify factors affecting efficiency, and use those findings to develop VPGTrans. Its two-stage framework aims to reuse the trained visual component when changing the language-model backbone. The practical question is how much of that earlier training can remain useful after the receiving model changes.

For transfer from BLIP-2 OPT 2.7B to BLIP-2 OPT 6.7B, the method uses less than 10% of the GPU hours and 10.7% of the training data required to train the target generator from scratch. The authors also build VL-LLaMA and VL-Vicuna using the approach. These examples demonstrate the potential for reusing visual-language components across different backbones with substantially lower training costs in the reported transfer.
neurips-2023-vpgtrans-transfer-visual-pr.tldr: VPGTrans transfers visual prompt generators between language models, substantially reducing training computation and data in a demonstrated transfer.
